title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus invalid-pch error on shared cmake_pch.hxx.gch
signature: cc1plus: error: cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API step fails compiling einsum.cpp with invalid-pch error

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation

key_errors: cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
root_cause: The ARM64 cross-compilation build uses precompiled headers (ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=ON) and sccache for distributed/remote compilation caching. The cmake_pch.hxx.gch precompiled header artifact becomes stale, truncated, or incompatible with the compiler invocation that consumes it (likely due to a cache race or a corrupted/partial sccache entry for the PCH generation step), so cc1plus rejects it as not a valid PCH file. Because -Werror=invalid-pch is enabled (via CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON), this otherwise-recoverable warning aborts the ninja build. This exact signature has now recurred 16 times across the last two weeks on this same ARM64 cross-compilation job, always in src/core/reference (einsum.cpp in this run, other objects in prior runs), confirming it is a build/cache infrastructure issue rather than a source-code regression tied to any specific commit.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally since it depends on sccache/PCH cache state. To approximate: build OpenVINO for aarch64 cross-compilation with -DENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=ON -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON and sccache enabled as the compiler launcher, then re-run the build after invalidating or truncating the sccache entry for cmake_pch.hxx.gch to simulate a corrupted PCH artifact.
recommended_actions: Disable or relax -Werror=invalid-pch for this configuration (or drop ENABLE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR for PCH-related diagnostics) so a stale PCH triggers a rebuild instead of a hard failure.

Investigate whether sccache is caching the generated cmake_pch.hxx.gch artifact itself and returning a corrupted/truncated copy; consider excluding PCH .gch outputs from sccache or verifying cache integrity before reuse.
Add a build-time check/retry that removes and regenerates cmake_pch.hxx.gch when cc1plus reports an invalid-pch error, instead of failing the whole build.
Given this has recurred 16 times, escalate to the CI/build infrastructure owners for the ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation runner/container image rather than treating each occurrence as a one-off.
prevention_strategies: Track PCH/sccache cache hit-rate and corruption metrics for the ARM64 cross-compilation job; add a cache-busting or integrity-verification step for precompiled headers before relying on them in a Werror build. Consider disabling ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD (PCH) specifically for this cross-compilation configuration until the underlying cache corruption is fixed.
historical_context: Identical signature first seen 2026-09-25 and recorded 15 times previously (pattern 0ee6d7327812b344), most recently 2026-10-06T16:50:38Z. This is now the 16th occurrence, all on the ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation Build job, consistently tied to the shared cmake_pch.hxx.gch precompiled header becoming invalid mid-build.
